articles.title: Solheim Cup golf 2026: Europe v USA, day two foursomes – live
articles.summary: ⛳️ Solheim Cup updates from 6.40am BST at Bernardus Golf ⛳️ Official live scoring | Day one report | And email Scott. Nelly Korda chops an awful tee shot wide right of the par-three 4th green. Team USA’s ball in deep heather.
body: Match three is getting increasingly volatile. Andrea Lee has the chance to win 9 from six feet but leaves her putt up on the high side. Mimi Rhodes can salvage a half from a very similar position, but learns nothing from Lee’s putt. Hole to the USA, and there’s a palpable sense of momentum slipping away from Europe. The hosts could do with someone winning a hole somewhere, just to shift things back on track.

The comeback is on! Oh it’s on! Nelly Korda walks in a 30-foot right-to-left slider on 11, and that’s a birdie-birdie start to the back nine for the five-and-o pair of Korda and Allisen Corpuz. Europe’s huge lead sliced in half in a matter of minutes!

Not for the first time this morning, Esther Henseleit makes a mess of a short putt. She misses to the right by the width of a ball from three feet on 9, and it costs Europe the chance to reduce the USA’s lead. Still no splitting these teams, with the projected score currently 6-6.

articles.title: Josh Addo-Carr allegedly records positive test for cocaine for second time
articles.summary: Parramatta Eels have notified NRL Integrity Unit over alleged incident. Veteran sacked by Bulldogs in 2024 after positive roadside drugs test. Veteran Parramatta winger Josh Addo-Carr has allegedly tested positive to cocaine for the second time in his NRL career after being pulled over by police…
body: Parramatta confirmed they were aware of an incident involving the 31-year-old, which reportedly happened in Sydney on Friday night.
“The Parramatta Eels are aware of an alleged incident involving Josh Addo-Carr,” the Eels said in a statement on Saturday afternoon.
“The club has notified the NRL Integrity Unit and is co-operating with the appropriate processes, as well as providing welfare support to Josh and his family.
“Parramatta Eels will not be commenting further until the matter has been finalised.”

articles.title: Garcia v Benn - welterweight world title fight predictions
articles.summary: Figures from the boxing world give their predictions for Saturday's WBC welterweight world title fight between Ryan Garcia and Briton Conor Benn.
body: Conor Benn returns to welterweight for the first time since April 2022 to challenge WBC champion Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas.
The 29-year-old Briton is bidding for the crowning moment of his 10-year professional career at T-Mobile Arena.
Benn has won 25 of his 26 fights as a professional and would emulate his father, Nigel, by claiming a WBC title with another victory.
Garcia, 28, is making the first defence of his belt after beating Mario Barrios by decision in February.

articles.title: ‘We are really different’: Matthew Brennan on ‘next Cavendish’ hype and his five-star Vuelta debut
articles.summary: Visma-Lease A Bike rider reflects on his stunning Grand Tour debut that has proved ‘the work had all been worth it’ When Matthew Brennan sat down with his team before the race to study this year’s Vuelta a España route, the young Briton had limited expectations for his Grand Tour debut.
body: He is also the youngest to win back-to-back stages. His fifth win was the seventh for his Visma‑Lease A Bike team in this Vuelta, the highest number they have ever achieved at this level, surpassing the tallies of six set at the 2022 Tour de France and this year’s Giro d’Italia.
Brennan’s has been one of the most remarkable Grand Tour debuts in history, and there’s a chance he may even take a sixth win in Sunday’s final stage in Granada.
As he has racked up the wins, the comparisons with the British sprint legend Mark Cavendish have become inevitable. Brennan is flattered but says he and the Manxman are not the same.

“It’s a really nice comparison, but we are really different riders,” he tells the Guardian after the Vuelta’s stage 18 time trial. “I can cope with stages that go up to three and a half thousand metres of climbing and still be there at the finish, while I don’t think that he would. But to be compared with such a savvy, classy rider is all good.”

articles.title: All change for Maresca: the data behind Manchester City’s rapid player turnover
articles.summary: Squad was a model of stability under Guardiola but many of the group the new coach oversees are recent recruits. Manchester City have experienced a level of player turnover unthinkable in the Pep Guardiola era.
body: Most people assumed City would demolish Coventry. Fantasy Premier League players set a record last weekend for the number who used their one-off option of triple-captaining a player to multiply his points by three. More than 91% used this bonus on Erling Haaland, expecting goals galore. He scored, but that was the only goal of the game. The match was closer than anyone anticipated.

Coventry’s chances were valued at 1.37 xG by Opta, suggesting they deserved to score. The more notable statistic was the visitors having 12 shots. Visitors to the Etihad hit that benchmark 17 times in the Premier League in a decade of Guardiola and none of those that did were newly promoted.

It is inevitable that a team containing many new players are less solid. City’s starting XI against Coventry was full of familiar names; it’s just that several are known for their achievements elsewhere.

articles.title: Benn makes weight - then puts on 32lbs in 12 hours
articles.summary: Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia both comfortably make the welterweight limit for their WBC title fight despite concerns at how they would fare on the scales.
body: Briton Benn, 29, weighed in at 10st 6lb (66kg) for Saturday's bout - half a pound heavier than the champion.
The official weigh-in took place behind closed doors at the UFC Apex on Friday, but only 12 hours later, Benn revealed on social media that he had put on 32lbs to reach 12st 10lb (81.65kg).
Speaking at a ceremonial event in front of fans later on Friday, Benn already looked noticeably bigger, his face and shoulders having filled out.
"Did it look hard? How did I look?," he asked. "We'll see tomorrow night how good I really feel."

articles.title: Signed instead of Rashford, Gordon is proving worth at Barca
articles.summary: Anthony Gordon's £70m move to Barcelona was questioned by some - but the England winger is already proving his worth for the free-scoring Spanish giants.
body: Anthony Gordon has only played five matches for Barcelona since joining in May, but the England winger is already making a big impression.
The former Newcastle United forward has provided four assists in his first five games for the free-scoring Spanish giants.
The 25-year-old is still hunting his first goal, but has slotted seamlessly into Barcelona's attack - in a left-wing spot often filled by on-loan England team-mate Marcus Rashford last term.
He delivered his welcome speech in Spanish - a language he said he learned with the help of one of Newcastle's Spanish physios - before adding a couple of phrases in Catalan when speaking with fans.

articles.title: Key reason why Barcelona rejected Marcus Rashford transfer despite 29 goal contributions
articles.summary: Journalist Fabrizio Romano reports that Barcelona’s decision to pass up the chance to sign Marcus Rashford permanently was not a result of his performances under Hansi Flick.
body: Rashford spent the 2025/26 campaign on loan from Manchester United and finished with 14 goals and 15 assists, contributing directly to 29 goals across all competitions.
Although he was not an automatic starter, the England international made a significant impact as Barcelona won both La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup.
Yet when the time came to decide on his long-term future, Barça opted for Anthony Gordon instead and Romano has explained that the choice was primarily driven by what Flick wanted from his attack.

Rather, the Barcelona manager respected the forward and developed a strong relationship with him during the season, so much so that his attitude and performances were viewed positively by the German coach.

articles.title: American Shelton to face Zverev in US Open final
articles.summary: Ben Shelton powers past Frances Tiafoe in an all-American US Open semi-final to earn a spot in Sunday's final against number one seed Alexander Zverev.
body: Ben Shelton powered his way into the US Open final with an impressive four-set win over Frances Tiafoe in an epic all-American semi-final.
Both players were bidding to reach their first Grand Slam final and put on a show for a raucous crowd on Arthur Ashe Stadium, with eighth seed Shelton coming from a set down to win 4-6 6-3 6-3 7-5.
Neither American was overawed by the occasion and they lived up to their reputations as dazzling shot-makers but, after three hours and 17 minutes, it was Shelton who won through.

The 23-year-old will face Alexander Zverev in Sunday's showpiece after the top seed beat unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov 6-3 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (8-6) to reach a third Grand Slam final in a row and continue his bid for a second major of the year.

articles.title: Frances Tiafoe admits what Ben Shelton did much better than him during their US Open semi-final
articles.summary: Frances Tiafoe saw his US Open title bid come to an end in the semi-finals against Ben Shelton. Tiafoe was beaten by Shelton, despite winning...
body: This was the third time that Tiafoe has lost in the semi-finals of the US Open, as his hope of becoming a Grand Slam champion has to wait another year.
When reflecting on his defeat to Shelton, Tiafoe admitted that there was something his compatriot did much better than him during the match.
Tiafoe reflected on his US Open run coming to an end in his post-match press conference, as he admitted he was not happy with the way he served, but was trying to take the positives from his season.

“We said it’s a tough one,” Tiafoe responded when asked what was said when speaking to his team after the match. “It’s hard. Obviously I have been in this position a lot now, thankfully, but also it’s tough. I wanted to be in a Grand Slam final, obviously, it is a big match.

body: Arsenal 's injury problems have been manageable, and they have not had to deal with the loss of an important player for a long period since the season started.

articles.title: Arteta details unusual methods for getting Arsenal players prepared
articles.summary: The Arsenal manager revealed that meals, transport and dressing-room routines have all been altered deliberately so the squad learns to adapt when plans go wrong. Photo by James Fearn/Getty Images.
body: Mikel Arteta has lifted the lid on one of the more unusual ways he prepares Arsenal for the unexpected, deliberately disrupting pre-season routines so his players are better equipped when plans go wrong for real.

The approach came into focus after Arsenal’s journey for their Champions League match away to Napoli was delayed by air-traffic-control problems in the UK. The disruption was significant enough to force the cancellation of Arteta’s scheduled pre-match media duties.
Arsenal still won 1-0 in Naples, and Arteta later explained that such problems were exactly the sort of thing he had tried to replicate during the summer.
“I love those challenges and I try to create them in preseason so when they happen, we already experience them and we are ready,” Arteta said.

articles.title: Nelson: Benn's graduation day is here but Garcia could be a class above
articles.summary: Conor Benn must prove he belongs at world level in this weekend's fight against Ryan Garcia, but the WBC champion might be too fast and too sharp, says Sky Sports expert Johnny Nelson.
body: Benn will challenge for his first world title when he takes on Garcia for the WBC welterweight belt at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas in the early hours of Sunday morning.
The Californian floored and outpointed Mario Barrios to become the new WBC champion in February, while he has previously fought elite champions such as Devin Haney and Gervonta Davis.
But Nelson is refusing to rule out a stunning victory for Benn.

"Never say never," Nelson told Sky Sports. "Right now, it seems like an impossible mountain to climb, because Conor Benn hasn't answered the questions that needed answering. Has he got that depth of experience? He hasn't. Can he dig deep? We know he can. Is he that level of a fighter? That's a question we don't know the answer to.
